notes:
Mid-market product org building an in-app onboarding copilot embedded in their web product. Primary ask: predictable sub-400ms token latency for streaming chat; reliable tool-calling (calendar/CRM write ops) with end-to-end success rates >99% for user flows. Cost sensitivity: token caps per user session, aggressive batching during bulk onboarding flows, want recommendations for per-route token limits.

AE summary: visited onsite demo (10/04), strong interest in Hosted API to get MVP out quickly, then switch to Dedicated if sustained usage. They repeatedly said: "can't have >500ms stalls during step-by-step onboarding". SE feedback: model outputs are OK for short prompts but hallucination on long multi-step instructions needs guardrails.

Legal/compliance: SOC2 baseline required, KMS integration for secrets, audit logs retention 1 year, potential EU residency requirement for a subset of customers later. Team asked for SSO test metadata and sample audit export.

Pricing sensitivity: mid-market budget but willing to commit for predictable latency; looking at 12- to 24-month reserved capacity if latency/cost numbers look right.

Tone of notes: short bullets, call paraphrases, action-focused.

requirements_summary: Workload: interactive in-app onboarding copilot (guided flows) + support chat fallback. Key targets: perceived latency p50 <200ms, p95 <400ms for streaming first-byte + continuous chunks; throughput target ~100 concurrent active users with spikes to 300 for product launches. Strong emphasis on streaming and tool-calling reliability (calendar/CRM writeback). Cost controls: per-session token caps, per-route token budget, intelligent batching for background re-renders. Model preference: high-quality 7B-13B quantized variants for cost balance; open to Redwood-verified optimized variants. Routing/fallback: prefer primary hosted endpoint with automatic fallback to lower-cost quantized variant; later evaluate Dedicated reserved pool for predictable tail latency. Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logging; possible data residency for EU customers down the road.
